name: Origins
tagline: Fourteen things to build, and one machine that becomes all of them.
hardware: Board: an Arduino-compatible UNO R3 with a CH340 USB chip. In the Arduino IDE it is Tools, Board, Arduino Uno.
Shield: Sensor Shield V4.0 on top of the board. Every pin has three rows: G (ground, black), V (power, red), S (signal, its own colour).
Power: the 2S Li-ion battery pack (7.4 V, two sealed cells, its own switch), plugged onto the shield's POWER pins, black on GND, red on VIN. The pack powers the machine.

The USB lead is for sending sketches. While it is plugged in, the board also runs from the computer. For the two week-long chapters (07 and the Doorkeeper), the USB lead goes into a phone charger instead.
The 9 V battery powers the lamp, through the switch board, and bench experiment 01. It is not rechargeable.

Shield rows used by the machine: 2 sensor A (black, red, blue), 3 dial power and its first signal (yellow), 4 dial (purple), 5 dial button (pink), 6 buzzer (magenta), 7 sensor B (light blue), 8 door switch (lime), 9 lamp switch board (grey), 11 light ring (cyan, with a 330 ohm resistor sealed in its lead), A4 and A5 the display (green SDA on A4, orange SCL on A5, brown power on POWER 3V3).
Free rows for the bench: 10, 12, 13, A0 and A1.
Sensors A and B are DHT22 temperature and humidity sensors. They are read every two seconds.
The display is a 0.96 inch OLED. It runs on 3.3 volts, so its power wire goes to 3V3, never 5 V.

The home screen, from chapter 01, shows three things: the reading, the number the maker is changing in that chapter, and what the machine decided. Row 0 is the decision (OK, COLD, ALARM ON, APART, TOO MANY, TOO DAMP and so on), shown reversed when it is an alarm. In chapters 02 to 08, 12 and the Doorkeeper the bottom row says what the ring, buzzer and lamp are doing, e.g. RING RED+BEEP. Chapter 09's screen leaves that row out on purpose, because chapters 10 and 11 run on it and chapter 11 gives no clues. From chapter 03, each sketch's whatTheScreenShows() function is exactly what its home screen shows: read the numbers and words from there.

The light ring is 8 WS2812B LEDs. The buzzer is a KY-006 passive buzzer: it plays notes. Its note is the maker's PITCH setting (200 to 4000 Hz, chosen on the dial from chapter 03). Cold beeps at that note, ALWAYS holds it, A and B apart plays a two-note siren, each door count plays a short higher note, TEST OUTPUTS plays three notes going up. The door switch is an MC-38 reed switch with a magnet. The switch board is an IRF520 MOSFET board. The lamp is a 12 V LED lamp on a 1 m lead.
Library: MakerNest Origins 1.1, from the IDE's Library Manager or the zip on the set-up page. It asks to install U8g2, Adafruit NeoPixel and DHT sensor library too: say yes.

Settings and the notebook live in the board's saved memory (EEPROM). Uploading a new sketch never clears them. From chapter 03 the last screen on the dial is RESET SETTINGS: press, turn to YES, press. Holding the dial down while pressing the shield's reset button does the same. Every setting goes back to how it came; the notebook is kept.

Chapter 09 adds WATCH FOR on the dial: COLD, HOT, DAMP or DRY. COLD and DRY go off when the reading goes under START and stop at STOP AT; HOT and DAMP go off when it goes over START and stop when it comes back down to STOP AT. DAMP and DRY watch sensor A's humidity in %. Choosing a new WATCH FOR clears START and STOP AT and opens START.
Every sketch uses 29 to 31.5 KB of the board's 32 KB. Chapter 12 and the Gift leave about 2.5 KB for the maker's own code.

Bench parts already in the box: a 170-point breadboard, 5 red LEDs, 5 × 10 kΩ resistors, 5 × 100 nF capacitors, 5 BC546 NPN transistors and jumper wires. The bench pack adds 2 light sensors (LDR), 2 push buttons, a yellow and a green LED, 10 × 220 Ω resistors, a KY-006 passive buzzer board, an SG90 servo and a soil sensor.
errata: The help table at the back of the book says 'the yellow wire is loose' for a number that never changes. Sensor A's signal wire is blue (row 2 S). Always say blue.
safety: Makers never open the battery pack. A grown-up charges it with the charger in the box, and nobody leaves it charging with nobody at home.
Never push anything metal into the pack or the shield while it is switched on.
If anything gets hot, smells of burning or looks scorched: switch the pack off, tell a grown-up, and email support@makernest.com.
Nothing in this kit needs mains electricity or soldering. Never suggest either.
The magnet and small parts stay out of mouths and away from small children.
